note: Draft 'build your plan' tasks for the block question (frontend only until the backend scores them). steps = the expected plan in order; traps = blocks that do not belong.

S1.q: Your washing machine breaks and the repair costs 1,500 zł. What steps would you take?
steps: Pay the repair from your emergency fund
Check how much is left in the fund
Top the fund back up over the next months
traps: Sell your investments in a hurry
Put it on a credit card and forget about it
S1.why: An emergency fund exists for exactly this. Use it, see what is left, then rebuild it slowly, so you never have to sell investments at a bad moment or borrow at high cost.

P4.q: Markets fall 30% in two months. Your plan is 60% shares and 40% bonds. What steps would you take?
steps: Check that your emergency fund is untouched
Remind yourself why you invested and for how long
Compare your current mix with the 60/40 plan
Rebalance back to 60/40 if it has drifted
traps: Sell all your shares to stop the losses
Move everything into the share that fell most
P4.why: A crash is when a plan earns its keep: make sure your safety net is fine, remember your horizon, and rebalance to the mix you chose instead of reacting to the news.

I5.q: You are choosing between two global index funds. What steps would you take?
steps: Check which index each fund follows
Decide how much to put in each month
traps: Pick the one that did best last year
Buy the one a friend recommended without checking
I5.why: The KID gives you the facts in a standard format. Costs and the index matter for the long run; last year's winner and tips from friends do not tell you much.
